q: 菜还没买___，我们再去一次超市吧。

context.rule: 动词 + 好: the action is done and done well, so you are ready
context.en: We haven't finished buying the food; let's go to the supermarket again.

why: Verb + 好 shows a job is done properly: 买好 means 'finished buying'.

not.远: 远 means 'far' and cannot describe the result of buying.
not.少: 少 means 'few' and 买少 does not mean 'finished buying'.
not.贵: 贵 means 'expensive' and is not a result of buying.

q: 明天的考试，我已经复习___了。

context.rule: 动词 + 好: the action is done and done well, so you are ready
context.en: I've already revised properly for tomorrow's exam.

why: Verb + 好 gives a done-properly result: 复习好了 means 'revised well'.

not.多: 多 means 'many' and does not fit as a result after 复习.
not.高: 高 means 'tall/high' and cannot follow 复习.
not.冷: 冷 means 'cold' and cannot follow 复习.

q: 电影票我昨天就买___了。

context.rule: 动词 + 好: the action is done and done well, so you are ready
context.en: I already bought the film tickets yesterday.

why: Verb + 好 means finished: 买好了 is 'bought it'.

not.长: 长 means 'long' and does not describe buying.
not.慢: 慢 means 'slow' and does not give the result 'done'.
not.白: 白 means 'white' and has no link to buying.

q: 行李已经准备___，我们可以走了。

context.rule: 动词 + 好: the action is done and done well, so you are ready
context.en: The luggage is all ready; we can go.

why: 准备好 means 'all ready': 行李已经准备好.

not.有: 有 means 'have' and is not a result complement.
not.是: 是 means 'be' and cannot follow a verb here.
not.在: 在 marks location, not the result of 准备.

q: 你的作业写___了吗？

context.rule: 动词 + 好: the action is done and done well, so you are ready
context.en: Have you finished your homework properly?

why: 写好 means 'written properly/finished': 作业写好了吗?

not.很: 很 is 'very' and cannot be a result after a verb.
not.太: 太 is 'too' and cannot be a result after 写.
not.和: 和 means 'and' and joins nouns, not a verb result.

q: 我一个字___不认识。

context.rule: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + 不/没 + verb: not even one, none at all
context.en: I don't know a single character.

why: 一 + measure word + 也 + 不 + verb means 'not even one': 一个字也不认识.

not.是: 是 means 'be'; 一个字是不认识 does not give 'not a single'.
not.很: 很 means 'very' and cannot replace 也 in this pattern.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and cannot replace 也 in this pattern.

q: 今天他一口饭___没吃。

context.rule: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + 不/没 + verb: not even one, none at all
context.en: He didn't eat a single mouthful today.

why: 一口饭都没吃 means 'did not eat a single mouthful'; 都 pairs with 没.

not.要: 要 means 'want', and 要没吃 is not possible.
not.会: 会 means 'can/will' and does not fit before 没吃.
not.在: 在 marks an action in progress and does not fit with 没吃.

q: 这件衣服一点儿也___贵。

context.rule: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + 不/没 + verb: not even one, none at all
context.en: This piece of clothing isn't expensive at all.

why: 一点儿也不贵 means 'not expensive at all'; 不 negates the adjective 贵.

not.没: 没 negates past events and 有, not an adjective like 贵.
not.很: 很 would turn it positive: 一点儿也很贵 is wrong.
not.太: 太 would turn it positive: 一点儿也太贵 is wrong.

q: 我昨天一杯水也___喝。

context.rule: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + 不/没 + verb: not even one, none at all
context.en: I didn't drink a single glass of water yesterday.

why: 一杯水也没喝 means 'did not drink a single glass'; 没 negates a past action.

not.很: 很 means 'very' and cannot negate the verb.
not.都: 都 would give 也都喝, which is not this pattern.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and cannot negate the verb.

q: 我今天一点儿钱也___，不能请你吃饭了。

context.rule: 一 + measure word + noun + 也/都 + 不/没 + verb: not even one, none at all
context.en: I have no money at all today, so I can't treat you to a meal.

why: 一点儿钱也没有 means 'no money at all'; 没有 is the negation needed.

not.不有: 不有 is not Chinese; the negative of 有 is 没有.
not.很有: 很有 would be positive: 'very much have'.
not.都有: 都有 means 'all have', the opposite meaning.

q: A：我不想去商店。 B：___我们在家看电影吧。

context.rule: 那 + result: “in that case…”, a conclusion from what was just said
context.en: A: I don't want to go to the shop. B: Then let's watch a film at home.

why: 那 at the start of a reply means 'then, in that case': 那我们在家看电影吧.

not.和: 和 means 'and' and cannot begin a reply.
not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, but this reply is a suggestion that follows from B's words.
not.虽然: 虽然 means 'although' and needs a 但是 clause.

q: A：明天下雨。 B：___我们不去爬山了。

context.rule: 那 + result: “in that case…”, a conclusion from what was just said
context.en: A: It will rain tomorrow. B: Then we won't go hiking.

why: 那 means 'in that case': since it will rain, 那我们不去爬山了.

not.和: 和 means 'and' and cannot open a sentence like this.
not.太: 太 is 'too' and needs an adjective after it.
not.还: 还 means 'still' and does not link to the previous statement.

q: A：我今天很累。 B：___你早点儿休息吧。

context.rule: 那 + result: “in that case…”, a conclusion from what was just said
context.en: A: I'm tired today. B: Then get some rest early.

why: 那 means 'in that case': since you're tired, 那你早点儿休息吧.

not.和: 和 means 'and' and does not open a reply.
not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts the logic here.
not.因为: 因为 gives a reason, but this sentence is advice.

q: A：这个太贵了。 B：___我们买那个便宜的吧。

context.rule: 那 + result: “in that case…”, a conclusion from what was just said
context.en: A: This one is too expensive. B: Then let's buy the cheaper one.

why: 那 means 'in that case': since it's too expensive, 那我们买那个便宜的吧.

not.和: 和 means 'and' and cannot open a reply.
not.因为: 因为 would give a reason without a result.
not.虽然: 虽然 means 'although' and needs 但是 later.

q: A：我已经吃过饭了。 B：___我们不用去饭馆了。

context.rule: 那 + result: “in that case…”, a conclusion from what was just said
context.en: A: I've already eaten. B: Then we don't need to go to a restaurant.

why: 那 means 'in that case': since you've eaten, 那我们不用去饭馆了.

not.和: 和 means 'and' and cannot open a reply.
not.但: 但 means 'but' and does not fit a logical conclusion.
not.还: 还 means 'still' and does not link to the previous statement.

q: 我在楼上等你，你快上___吧。

context.point: 来 / 去 after a verb
context.rule: V + 来 / 去: 来 = towards the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker; a place goes before 来/去
context.en: I'm waiting upstairs. Come on up.

why: 上来 means 'come up' toward the speaker, who is upstairs: 你快上来吧.

not.去: 去 means 'go' away from the speaker, but the speaker is upstairs.
not.过: 过 marks experience or passing by, not direction here.
not.回: 回 means 'return', which is not about going upstairs.

q: 我现在在公司，下了班就回家___。

context.point: 来 / 去 after a verb
context.rule: V + 来 / 去: 来 = towards the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker; a place goes before 来/去
context.en: I'm at the company now; after work I'll go home.

why: 回家去 means 'go home' (away from the speaker at the company).

not.来: 在 is a preposition and cannot end the clause after 回家.
not.在: 把 starts a 把 sentence and cannot end the clause.
not.把: 来 would mean coming toward the speaker, but the speaker is at the company.

q: 我在办公室里，你在外边吧？我出___找你。

context.point: 来 / 去 after a verb
context.rule: V + 来 / 去: 来 = towards the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker; a place goes before 来/去
context.en: I'm in the office and you're outside, right? I'll come out to find you.

why: 出去 means 'go out' away from the speaker, who is in the office.

not.来: 来 means 'come' toward the speaker, but the speaker stays inside.
not.回: 回 means 'return' and doesn't fit 出___找你.
not.过: 过 means 'cross/pass' and does not fit this direction.

q: 老师在教室里等你，我们在外边，你快进___吧。

context.point: 来 / 去 after a verb
context.rule: V + 来 / 去: 来 = towards the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker; a place goes before 来/去
context.en: The teacher is waiting in the classroom and we're outside. Go in quickly.

why: 进去 means 'go in', away from the speakers who are outside.

not.来: 来 would mean coming toward the speakers, but they are outside.
not.出: 出 means 'out', the opposite of going in.
not.过: 过 means 'cross/pass' and does not fit 进___吧.

q: 妈妈进___来叫我吃饭了。

context.point: 来 / 去 after a verb
context.rule: V + 来 / 去: 来 = towards the speaker, 去 = away from the speaker; a place goes before 来/去
context.en: Mum came into the room to call me for dinner.

why: 进房间来 puts the place 房间 between 进 and 来: 妈妈进房间来.

not.汉语: 汉语 is a language, not a place you can enter.
not.面包: 面包 means 'bread', not a place to enter.
not.休息: 休息 is a verb and cannot follow 进 as a place.

q: 他下了课___去图书馆。

context.rule: V1 了 + (subject) + 就 + V2: the second action follows right after the first
context.en: As soon as he finishes class he goes to the library.

why: V1 了 ... 就 V2: after finishing class, he goes at once. 下了课就去.

not.要: 要 means 'want' and does not show one action right after another.
not.和: 和 means 'and' and joins nouns, not actions.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and needs an adjective.

q: 妈妈回了家___做饭。

context.rule: V1 了 + (subject) + 就 + V2: the second action follows right after the first
context.en: As soon as mum gets home she cooks.

why: V1 了 ... 就 V2: 回了家就做饭 means 'cooks as soon as she gets home'.

not.很: 很 means 'very' and does not link two actions.
not.不: 不 negates a verb and does not link actions in time.

q: 我吃___饭就去睡觉。

context.rule: V1 了 + (subject) + 就 + V2: the second action follows right after the first
context.en: I'll go to sleep right after I eat.

why: V1 了 + object + 就 V2: 吃了饭就去睡觉 means 'right after eating'.

not.得: 得 links a verb to a complement of degree, not completion.
not.吗: 吗 makes a question, but this is a statement.

q: 你到了机场我___去接你。

context.rule: V1 了 + (subject) + 就 + V2: the second action follows right after the first
context.en: As soon as you get to the airport I'll come and pick you up.

why: 到了 ... 就: when you arrive, I'll pick you up at once; 就 links the two actions.

not.很: 很 means 'very' and does not link two actions.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and needs an adjective.
not.不: 不 would negate 去接你, which changes the meaning.

q: 爸爸回了家，我们___吃饭。

context.rule: V1 了 + (subject) + 就 + V2: the second action follows right after the first
context.en: As soon as dad gets home, we'll eat.

why: V1 了 ... 就 V2: after dad gets home, we eat right away.

not.太: 太 means 'too' and cannot link two actions.
not.把: 把 begins an object phrase and does not link time.
not.很: 很 means 'very' and does not link two actions.

q: 你天天不运动，___不胖吗？

context.point: 能……吗 as a rhetorical question
context.rule: 能 + positive + 吗 means “no way”; 能 + negative + 吗 means “of course”
context.en: You never exercise; how could you not get fat?

why: 能 + 不 + adjective + 吗 is a rhetorical question: 能不胖吗? means 'how could you not get fat?'

not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not form this question.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and cannot precede 不胖.
not.为: 为 needs a pattern like 为什么 and does not mean 'can' here.

q: 这么难的题，我___做对吗？

context.point: 能……吗 as a rhetorical question
context.rule: 能 + positive + 吗 means “no way”; 能 + negative + 吗 means “of course”
context.en: Such a hard question; how could I get it right?

why: 能 ... 吗 asks 'how could I?' as a rhetorical question: 我能做对吗?

not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 做对.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not mean 'can'.
not.在: 在 marks location or an ongoing action, not ability.

q: 天这么冷，你___不穿衣服吗？

context.point: 能……吗 as a rhetorical question
context.rule: 能 + positive + 吗 means “no way”; 能 + negative + 吗 means “of course”
context.en: It's so cold; could you really go without clothes?

why: 能不穿衣服吗 is a rhetorical question: 'can you really go without clothes?'

not.在: 在 marks an ongoing action, but this needs the modal 能.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not take 不穿.
not.和: 和 means 'and' and cannot be a modal verb.

q: 你一直玩游戏，作业___写完吗？

context.point: 能……吗 as a rhetorical question
context.rule: 能 + positive + 吗 means “no way”; 能 + negative + 吗 means “of course”
context.en: You keep playing games; how could the homework get finished?

why: 能 + 写完 + 吗 is a rhetorical question: 作业能写完吗? means 'how could it get done?'

not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not fit before 写完.
not.在: 在 marks an ongoing action and does not give this meaning.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 写完.

q: 他每天都复习，考试___不好吗？

context.point: 能……吗 as a rhetorical question
context.rule: 能 + positive + 吗 means “no way”; 能 + negative + 吗 means “of course”
context.en: He revises every day; of course the exam will go well.

why: 能不好吗 is a rhetorical question meaning 'of course it will be good'.

not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not form this question.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and cannot precede 不好.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and needs a direction.

q: 你想喝茶___喝咖啡？

context.rule: 还是 for choices in questions (and inside “I don't know whether…” clauses); 或者 for choices in statements
context.en: Do you want tea or coffee?

why: 还是 offers a choice in a question: 茶还是咖啡?

not.或者: 或者 is used in statements, not in questions asking for a choice.
not.因为: 因为 means 'because' and does not offer a choice.
not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and does not offer a choice.

q: 你可以坐公共汽车___坐地铁去。

context.rule: 还是 for choices in questions (and inside “I don't know whether…” clauses); 或者 for choices in statements
context.en: You can go by bus or by metro.

why: 或者 offers alternatives in a statement: 坐公共汽车或者坐地铁.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and contrasts rather than offers a choice.
not.因为: 因为 means 'because' and gives a reason.
not.所以: 所以 means 'so' and gives a result.

q: 我还没想好明天去爬山___去游泳。

context.rule: 还是 for choices in questions (and inside “I don't know whether…” clauses); 或者 for choices in statements
context.en: I haven't decided whether to go hiking or swimming tomorrow.

why: 还是 offers a choice that is not decided yet: 爬山还是游泳.

not.或者: 或者 is for statements, but 没想好 leaves an open choice between two options.
not.因为: 因为 means 'because' and does not offer a choice.
not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and contrasts rather than offers a choice.

q: 他是你哥哥___你弟弟？

context.rule: 还是 for choices in questions (and inside “I don't know whether…” clauses); 或者 for choices in statements
context.en: Is he your older brother or your younger brother?

why: 还是 joins two options in a question: 哥哥还是弟弟?

not.或者: 或者 is used in statements, not in this question.
not.和: 和 joins things together, but a choice needs 还是.
not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and does not offer a choice.

q: 我想吃面包___米饭，都可以。

context.rule: 还是 for choices in questions (and inside “I don't know whether…” clauses); 或者 for choices in statements
context.en: I'd like bread or rice; either is fine.

why: 或者 means 'or' in a statement: 面包或者米饭, either is fine.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and contrasts instead of giving a choice.
not.因为: 因为 means 'because' and gives a reason.
not.所以: 所以 means 'so' and gives a result.

q: 冰箱里放___很多鸡蛋。

context.rule: Location + 放/住/写/坐 + 着 + indefinite noun: there is something somewhere; negative: 没 + V着
context.en: There are lots of eggs in the fridge.

why: Place + V着 + something describes what is there: 冰箱里放着很多鸡蛋.

not.在: 在 marks location, and 放在 would need a place after it.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit here.
not.给: 给 means 'give' and does not describe a state.

q: 床上___着一只小猫。

context.rule: Location + 放/住/写/坐 + 着 + indefinite noun: there is something somewhere; negative: 没 + V着
context.en: A kitten is sleeping on the bed.

why: Place + V着 + something: a kitten is sleeping there. 床上睡着一只小猫.

not.吃: 吃着 would need food as the thing; a kitten isn't being eaten on the bed.
not.买: 买 means 'buy' and does not describe a state with 着.
not.看: 看着 would not describe a kitten lying on the bed.

q: 教室里坐___很多学生。

context.rule: Location + 放/住/写/坐 + 着 + indefinite noun: there is something somewhere; negative: 没 + V着
context.en: Many students are sitting in the classroom.

why: Place + V着 + something: 教室里坐着很多学生.

not.在: 在 marks location, and 坐在 would need a place after it.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit here.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not mark a state.

q: 我家旁边住着___医生。

context.rule: Location + 放/住/写/坐 + 着 + indefinite noun: there is something somewhere; negative: 没 + V着
context.en: A doctor lives next door to me.

why: 住着一个医生: a doctor lives there. 一个 introduces a new person.

not.这个: 这个 means 'this' and points to a known person, but this introduces someone new.
not.那个: 那个 means 'that' and points to a known person, not a new one.
not.是: 是 means 'be' and 住着是医生 does not work.

q: 书包里没___书。

context.rule: Location + 放/住/写/坐 + 着 + indefinite noun: there is something somewhere; negative: 没 + V着
context.en: There are no books in the schoolbag.

why: 没放着书 is the negative of 放着 (a state): 书包里没放着书.

not.放了: 放了 is for a finished action, and 没放了 is wrong.
not.着放: 着放 has the wrong word order.
not.放在: 放在 needs a place after it, not 书.

q: 你穿这么少，___感冒的。

context.rule: 会 + verb (+ 的): something is likely to happen
context.en: You're wearing so little; you'll catch a cold.

why: 会 shows something likely to happen: 你会感冒的.

not.在: 在 marks an ongoing action and does not show a possibility.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 感冒.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not show a possibility.

q: 别着急，他很快就___来的。

context.rule: 会 + verb (+ 的): something is likely to happen
context.en: Don't worry; he'll be here soon.

why: 会 ... 的 shows a prediction: 他很快就会来的.

not.在: 在 marks an ongoing action, but he hasn't arrived yet.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit here.
not.让: 让 means 'let/make' and needs a person after it.

q: 坐在这把椅子上___很舒服的。

context.rule: 会 + verb (+ 的): something is likely to happen
context.en: You'll be comfortable sitting in this chair.

why: 会 ... 的 expresses a prediction: 你会很舒服的.

not.在: 在 marks an ongoing action and does not predict.
not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 很舒服.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not predict.

q: 你不早点儿睡觉，明天___很累的。

context.rule: 会 + verb (+ 的): something is likely to happen
context.en: If you don't sleep early, you'll be tired tomorrow.

why: 会 ... 的 expresses a prediction: 明天会很累的.

not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 很累.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not predict.
not.给: 给 means 'give' and does not predict.

q: 天气预报说明天___下雪。

context.rule: 会 + verb (+ 的): something is likely to happen
context.en: The forecast says it will snow tomorrow.

why: 会 + verb says what will happen: 明天会下雪.

not.把: 把 begins a 把 sentence and does not fit before 下雪.
not.对: 对 means 'toward/correct' and does not mean 'will'.
not.给: 给 means 'give' and does not mean 'will'.

q: 这个苹果又红___甜。

context.rule: 又 + adjective + 又 + adjective: both … and … (two qualities at once)
context.en: This apple is both red and sweet.

why: 又……又…… joins two qualities: 又红又甜.

not.也: 也 means 'also' and does not form the 又A又B pattern.
not.很: 很 means 'very' and does not link two adjectives.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and cannot link two adjectives.

q: 这家饭馆的菜又多___好吃。

context.rule: 又 + adjective + 又 + adjective: both … and … (two qualities at once)
context.en: The dishes in this restaurant are both generous and tasty.

why: 又……又…… joins two qualities: 又多又好吃.

not.就: 就 means 'then/just' and does not link two adjectives.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and cannot link two adjectives.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and does not link two adjectives.

q: 小明又聪明___努力，老师很喜欢他。

context.rule: 又 + adjective + 又 + adjective: both … and … (two qualities at once)
context.en: Xiaoming is both clever and hard-working; the teacher likes him a lot.

why: 又……又…… joins two qualities of one person: 又聪明又努力.

not.和: 和 means 'and' but this pattern needs 又 before each adjective.
not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and contrasts instead of adding.
not.因为: 因为 means 'because' and does not link two adjectives.

q: 他做饭做得又快___好。

context.rule: 又 + adjective + 又 + adjective: both … and … (two qualities at once)
context.en: He cooks both fast and well.

why: 又……又…… joins two qualities: 又快又好.

not.和: 和 means 'and' but 又快和好 is not the pattern.
not.很: 很 means 'very' and does not link two adjectives.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and does not link two adjectives.

q: 外边又黑___冷，我们别出去了。

why: 左右 after a quantity means 'about': 二十个学生左右 is 'about twenty students'.

not.几: 几 asks or means 'a few' and goes before the measure word, not after 学生.
not.多了: 多了 means 'much more' after an adjective; it doesn't mean 'about'.
not.一点儿: 一点儿 means 'a little' and doesn't work after 学生.

q: 这个电脑要五千块___。

context.rule: 左右 comes after a number or quantity to say "about" or "or so".
context.en: This computer costs around five thousand yuan.

why: 左右 after an amount means 'about': 五千块左右 is 'around 5,000 yuan'.

not.比较: 比较 means 'fairly' and goes before an adjective, not after an amount.
not.一样: 一样 means 'the same' and needs something to compare with.
not.附近: 附近 means 'nearby' and goes with places, not prices.

q: 他三十岁___，个子很高。

context.rule: 左右 comes after a number or quantity to say "about" or "or so".
context.en: He is about thirty and quite tall.

why: 三十岁左右 means 'about thirty years old'; 左右 follows the number.

not.以前的: 以前的 means 'earlier' or 'former' and can't follow 三十岁 to mean 'about'.
not.多了: 多了 means 'much more' and doesn't give 'about'.
not.比较: 比较 means 'fairly' and goes before an adjective, not after an age.

q: 我每天走路二十分钟___。

context.rule: 左右 comes after a number or quantity to say "about" or "or so".
context.en: I walk about twenty minutes every day.

why: 二十分钟左右 means 'about twenty minutes'; 左右 follows the amount.

not.的: 的 can't follow 二十分钟 to say 'about'.
not.比: 比 compares two things; nothing is compared here.
not.先: 先 means 'first' and goes before a verb, not after an amount.

q: 下午三点___，请给我打电话。

context.rule: 左右 comes after a number or quantity to say "about" or "or so".
context.en: Please call me around three in the afternoon.

why: 三点左右 means 'around three o'clock'; 左右 follows the time.

not.不太: 不太 means 'not very' and goes before an adjective, not after a time.
not.又: 又 means 'again' and goes before a verb.
not.越: 越 is used in 越来越 or 越……越……, not after a time.

q: 他七点___到学校了，比老师还早。

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: He got to school as early as seven, even before the teacher.

why: 七点就到学校了: 就 shows it was early, so he arrived even before the teacher.

not.才: 才 means 'only then' and shows late; it doesn't fit 'even before the teacher'.
not.又: 又 means 'again', but he did not arrive twice.
not.再: 再 means 'again' later; this is a past event.

q: 电影七点开始，她七点半___到。

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: The film started at seven, and she didn't arrive until half past.

why: 她七点半才到: 才 shows it was later than expected.

not.又: 又 means 'again'; her arriving is not a repeat.
not.再: 再 means 'again' for a future action, not 'only then'.
not.常: 常 means 'often' and doesn't show lateness.

q: 这个字很简单，我看了一次___会写了。

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: This character is simple; I could write it after seeing it once.

why: 看了一次就会写了: 就 shows it took little effort, so it was quick.

not.才: 才 would mean it took a long time, the opposite of the meaning.
not.再: 再 means 'again' for a later action; this is already done.
not.还: 还 means 'still' or 'also'; it doesn't show quickness.

q: 这本书很难，我看了一个月___看完。

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: This book is hard; it took me a whole month to finish it.

why: 看了一个月才看完: 才 shows it took a long time before it finished.

not.再: 再 means 'again' for a later action.
not.又: 又 means 'again' for a repeated action.
not.还: 还 means 'still'; it doesn't show 'only after a long time'.

q: 我等了他一个小时，他___来。

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: I waited an hour for him before he finally came.

why: 等了一个小时，他才来: 才 shows he came late, after a long wait.

not.都: 都 means 'all' or 'even' and doesn't show lateness.
not.先: 先 means 'first' and doesn't show lateness.
not.又: 又 means 'again'; his coming isn't a repeat.

q: 现在才八点，你怎么___要走了？

context.rule: Both go before the verb. 就 shows the speaker thinks something happens early, quickly or easily; 才 shows it happens late, slowly or with difficulty.
context.en: It's only eight; why are you leaving already?

why: 现在才八点，你怎么就要走了: 就 shows it is early, so leaving feels too soon.

not.才: 才 would repeat 'only' and shows late, which clashes with 要走了.
not.还: 还要走了 doesn't give the meaning 'already leaving'.

q: 请把书放___桌子上。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: Please put the book on the table.

why: 把书放在桌子上: 在 follows 放 to say where the book ends up.

not.给: 给 means 'to' a person receiving something; the object here goes to a place.
not.对: 对 means 'towards / to' a person and does not follow a verb after 把.
not.从: 从 means 'from', but the sentence needs a destination or recipient.

q: 我把这封信寄___朋友了。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: I posted the letter to a friend.

why: 我把这封信寄给朋友了: 给 follows 寄 to say who received it.

not.在: 在 marks a place; 朋友 is a person.
not.从: 从 means 'from', but the sentence needs a destination or recipient.
not.比: 比 compares two things; it cannot follow the verb here.

q: 朋友把我送___火车站。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: My friend took me to the railway station.

why: 朋友把我送到火车站: 到 follows 送 to say the destination.

not.给: 给 marks a person who receives something; 火车站 is a place.
not.在: 在 marks where something stays, not where someone is taken.
not.对: 对 means 'towards / to' a person and does not follow a verb after 把.

q: 他把照片放___我的包里了。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: He put the photos in my bag.

why: 他把照片放在我的包里了: 在 follows 放 to say where the photos ended up.

not.给: 给 means 'to' a person receiving something; the object here goes to a place.
not.对: 对 means 'towards / to' a person and does not follow a verb after 把.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and is not used after the verb in a 把 sentence this way.

q: 请你把这本书拿___图书馆去。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: Please take this book to the library.

why: 请你把这本书拿到图书馆去: 到 follows 拿 to say where the book goes.

not.给: 给 marks a person who receives something; 图书馆 is a place.
not.在: 在 marks where something stays, not where it is taken.
not.对: 对 means 'towards / to' a person and does not follow a verb after 把.

q: 我把礼物送___妈妈了。

context.point: A 把 B + verb + 在 / 到 / 给 + place or person
context.rule: This 把 pattern says that something is moved to a place or handed to someone.
context.en: I gave the present to Mum.

why: 我把礼物送给妈妈了: 给 follows 送 to say who gets the present.

not.在: 在 marks a place; 妈妈 is a person.
not.到: 到 marks a destination place; 妈妈 is a person.
not.从: 从 means 'from', but the sentence needs a destination or recipient.

q: 小狗从房间里跑___来了。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: The puppy ran out of the room.

why: 跑出来: 出 + 来 means coming out toward the speaker; the puppy ran out of the room.

not.进: 进 means 'into', but 从房间里 shows it came out.
not.上: 上 means 'up', not 'out of a room'.
not.下: 下 means 'down', not 'out of a room'.

q: 我在房间里，妈妈走进房间___了。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: I'm in the room, and Mum has walked in.

why: 走进房间来: 来 shows the movement is toward the speaker, who is in the room.

not.去: 去 means moving away from the speaker; Mum comes toward me.
not.出: 出 means 'out', but she walked in.
not.回: 回 means 'back' and doesn't fit after 房间 here.

q: 我在家里，爸爸走出家门___了。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: I'm at home, and Dad has walked out of the door.

why: 走出家门去: 去 shows Dad moves away from the speaker, who is at home.

not.来: 来 means toward the speaker; Dad went away from me.
not.起: 起 needs 来 and doesn't fit after 家门.
not.里: 里 means 'inside' and isn't a direction complement here.

q: 看了一天书了，你站___走走吧。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: You've been reading all day; stand up and walk about a bit.

why: 站起来: 起来 after 站 means 'stand up'.

not.上来: 上来 means 'come up', not 'rise from sitting'.
not.进来: 进来 means 'come in', not 'stand up'.
not.出去: 出去 means 'go out', not 'stand up'.

q: 我在家里，妹妹从超市拿回___两瓶牛奶。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: I'm at home, and my sister has brought two bottles of milk back from the supermarket.

why: 拿回来: 回 + 来 means bringing back toward the speaker, who is at home.

not.去: 去 means moving away from the speaker; she brought it to me.
not.出: 出 means 'out' and doesn't fit 拿回___.
not.过: 过 means 'over / across' and doesn't fit 拿回___.

q: 哥哥从北京寄___来一些照片。

context.point: Compound direction complements: verb + 出 / 回 / 进 / 起 / 过 + 来 or 去
context.rule: A verb plus a direction word plus 来 (towards the speaker) or 去 (away from the speaker). A place object goes between the two parts.
context.en: My brother has posted some photos back from Beijing.

why: 寄回来: 回 + 来 means sent back toward the speaker; 一些照片 sent from Beijing.

not.起: 起 only works in 起来 and doesn't fit 寄___来.
not.下: 下 means 'down' and doesn't suit sending something back.
not.上: 上 means 'up' and doesn't suit sending something back.

q: 我喜欢一边听音乐，___做作业。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: I like to listen to music while doing homework.

why: 一边……，一边……: 一边听音乐，一边做作业 means doing two things at once.

not.一起: 一起 means 'together' and doesn't join two actions.
not.一下: 一下 means 'a bit' after a verb.

q: 我和朋友一边喝咖啡，___聊天儿。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: My friend and I chatted while drinking coffee.

why: 一边……，一边……: 一边喝咖啡，一边聊天儿 means doing two things at once.

not.一起: 一起 means 'together' and doesn't join two actions.

q: 你不要一边开车___打电话。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: Don't make phone calls while driving.

why: 不要一边开车一边打电话: 一边……一边…… links two actions at once.

q: 妈妈___做饭一边跟我说话。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: Mum chats with me while she cooks.

why: 妈妈一边做饭一边跟我说话: the first 一边 pairs with the second one.

not.一般: 一般 means 'usually' and doesn't pair with 一边.

q: 他喜欢一边走路，一边___音乐。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: He likes to listen to music while walking.

why: 一边走路，一边听音乐: after 一边 you need a bare verb, 听.

not.一听: 一听 means 'hear it once' and can't follow 一边.
not.听了: 听了 marks a finished action; 一边 needs a bare verb.
not.听着听: 听着听 is not a pattern.

q: 妹妹边唱___跳，玩儿得很高兴。

context.rule: Two actions happening at the same time. The first 一 can be dropped.
context.en: My sister sang and danced at the same time, having great fun.

why: 边唱边跳 is the short form of 一边唱一边跳: doing both at once.

not.也: 也 means 'also'; 边唱也跳 is not this pattern.
not.就: 就 means 'then / right away' and doesn't pair with 边.
not.再: 再 means 'again / then' and doesn't pair with 边.

q: 我把盘子洗___了。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: I've washed the plates clean.

why: 洗干净: 干净 after the verb tells the result, so the plates are clean.

not.高兴: 高兴 means 'happy' and can't be the result of washing plates.
not.安静: 安静 means 'quiet', not a result of washing.
not.方便: 方便 means 'convenient', not a result of washing.

q: 我还没把作业写___呢。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: I haven't finished my homework yet.

why: 写好: 好 after 写 means the writing is done properly; 还没……呢 says not yet.

not.高: 高 means 'tall' and can't be a result of writing.
not.长: 长 means 'long' and isn't the result meant here.
not.远: 远 means 'far' and doesn't suit 写.

q: 我在楼下，你把伞拿___吧。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: I'm downstairs; bring the umbrella down to me.

why: 拿下来: 下来 means bringing it down toward the speaker, who is downstairs.

not.上去: 上去 means going up away from the speaker, but I'm downstairs.
not.进去: 进去 means 'go in', not 'come down'.
not.过去: 过去 means 'go over', not 'come down'.

q: 你把这个节目看___就去写作业。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: Finish watching this programme and then go and do your homework.

why: 把这个节目看完: 完 after 看 means finished watching.

not.的: 的 can't follow a verb to give a result.
not.地: 地 links an adverb to a verb; it can't be a result.
not.得: 得 links a verb to a degree or result phrase; it is not a complement here.

q: 别着急，我把你的行李搬___房间里去了。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: Don't worry, I carried your luggage into the room.

why: 搬进房间里去: 进 + 去 means carrying the luggage into the room.

not.出: 出 means 'out', but the luggage goes into the room.
not.上: 上 means 'up' and doesn't fit 房间里.
not.下: 下 means 'down' and doesn't fit 房间里.

q: 请你把窗户打___。

context.point: 把 + object + verb + result or direction complement
context.rule: The thing handled is put after 把; the verb is followed by a complement that says the result (好, 干净, 完) or the direction (出来, 过去).
context.en: Please open the window.

why: 把窗户打开: 开 after 打 means the window ends up open.

not.去: 去 means 'go' and isn't the result of 打开.
not.近: 近 means 'near'; windows aren't opened that way.
not.高: 高 means 'tall' and isn't a result of 打.

q: 起床以后，我___洗澡，然后吃早饭。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: After I get up I take a shower first, then have breakfast.

why: 先洗澡，然后吃早饭: 先 starts the first step in the order.

not.又: 又 means 'again' and doesn't start a sequence.
not.再: 再 means 'then' for the later step, not the first.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and shows lateness, not a first step.

q: 你先把饭吃完，然后___出去玩儿。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: Finish your meal first, then go out and play.

why: 先……，然后再……: 再 follows 然后 to mean 'after that, then'.

not.又: 又 means 'again' for a past event; this is a future instruction.
not.把: 把 can't stand here; 出去玩儿 needs no object.

q: 昨天我先去了超市，___去了图书馆。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: Yesterday I went to the supermarket first, then to the library.

why: 先去了……，又去了……: 又 links a second past action after the first.

not.再: 再 is used for future actions; 去了 here is past.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't suit a simple next step.
not.先: 先 would start a new sequence, but 先 was already used.

q: 你先把桌子擦干净，然后___把盘子放上去。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: Wipe the table clean first, then put the plates on it.

why: 先……，然后再……: 再把盘子放上去 is the later step in a future order.

not.又: 又 is for a past or repeated action, not a future step.
not.已经: 已经 means 'already' and doesn't fit a plan.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and doesn't link steps.

q: 明天我先去图书馆，___去超市。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: Tomorrow I'll go to the library first and then the supermarket.

why: 先去图书馆，然后去超市: 然后 links the first step to the next.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and doesn't link steps.

q: 我先洗了澡，然后___看了一会儿电视。

context.rule: First…, then…, after that…. 再 is for actions that have not happened yet; 又 is for ones that have.
context.en: I took a shower first, and then watched TV for a while.

why: 先洗了澡，然后又看了一会儿电视: 又 adds a second past action.

not.再: 再 is for future actions; 看了 is past.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and doesn't link steps.
not.要: 要 means 'want / will' and doesn't fit 看了.

q: ___这本书以外，别的书我都看过。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，都 …: everyone/everything except A does it
context.en: I've read every book except this one.

why: 除了……以外，别的书我都看过: 除了 means 'except' and pairs with 以外.

q: 除了小李以外，其他同学___来了。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，都 …: everyone/everything except A does it
context.en: Everyone except Xiao Li has come.

why: 除了小李以外，其他同学都来了: 都 covers everyone apart from the exception.

not.还: 还 adds 'also', which means 'besides', not 'everyone else'.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't cover everyone.

q: 我们学校除了王老师，其他老师___是男的。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，都 …: everyone/everything except A does it
context.en: In our school, all the teachers except Teacher Wang are men.

why: 除了王老师，其他老师都是男的: 都 covers all the others besides the exception.

not.还: 还 means 'also', but the sentence needs 'all'.
not.就: 就 means 'then / just' and doesn't cover everyone.

q: 除了周末，我___天都要上班。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，都 …: everyone/everything except A does it
context.en: Except at weekends, I work every day.

why: 每天 means 'every day': 除了周末，我每天都要上班.

not.各: 各 means 'each' and goes before a measure word, not 天.
not.多: 多天 means 'many days', not 'every day'.
not.这: 这天 means 'this day', not 'every day'.

q: ___他以外，我们都去过长城。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，都 …: everyone/everything except A does it
context.en: Apart from him, all of us have been to the Great Wall.

why: 除了他以外，我们都去过长城: 除了 means 'except', with 都 after it.

q: 除了咖啡以外，他___喜欢喝茶。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，还 B: A and also B
context.en: Besides coffee, he also likes tea.

why: 除了咖啡以外，他还喜欢喝茶: 还 adds something besides the coffee.

not.都: 都 means 'all', but this sentence adds tea, not 'all'.
not.就: 就 means 'then / just' and doesn't add.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't add.

q: 除了英语，我___会说汉语。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，还 B: A and also B
context.en: Besides English, I can speak Chinese too.

why: 除了英语，我还会说汉语: 还 adds Chinese besides English.

not.都: 都 means 'all', but this adds one more language.
not.再: 再 means 'again' and doesn't add here.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't add.

q: 除了唱歌，她___会跳舞。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，还 B: A and also B
context.en: Besides singing, she can dance too.

why: 除了唱歌，她也会跳舞: 也 adds dancing besides singing.

not.都: 都 means 'all', but this adds one more skill.
not.再: 再 means 'again' and doesn't add here.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't add.

q: 除了打篮球，他还喜欢___。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，还 B: A and also B
context.en: Besides basketball, he likes swimming too.

why: 除了打篮球，他还喜欢游泳: 还喜欢 needs a bare verb 游泳 after it.

not.游泳了: 游泳了 marks a finished action, not a liking.
not.在游泳: 在游泳 means 'is swimming right now'.
not.游泳的: 游泳的 means 'the one who swims' and leaves 喜欢 incomplete.

q: 除了这件衣服以外，我___买了一条裤子。

context.rule: 除了 A 以外，还 B: A and also B
context.en: Besides this piece of clothing, I also bought a pair of trousers.

why: 除了这件衣服以外，我还买了一条裤子: 还 adds another item.

not.都: 都 means 'all', but this adds one more item.
not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't add.
not.就: 就 means 'then / just' and doesn't add.

q: 你想不想吃点儿___？

context.rule: 有没有什么 …: “什么” makes a question softer, and the sentence means the same without it
context.en: Would you like something to eat?

why: 什么 here is soft and indefinite: 吃点儿什么 means 'something to eat'.

not.谁: 谁 means 'who' and can't be eaten.
not.哪儿: 哪儿 means 'where' and doesn't fit after 吃点儿.
not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and doesn't fit after 吃点儿.

q: 你的作业有没有___问题？

context.rule: 有没有什么 …: “什么” makes a question softer, and the sentence means the same without it
context.en: Are there any problems with your homework?

why: 什么 means 'any' in 有没有什么问题: 'any problems at all'.

not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and doesn't go before 问题.
not.多少: 多少 asks 'how many' and doesn't fit 有没有.
not.几: 几 asks 'how many (small number)' and needs a measure word.

q: 你有没有___要买的东西？

context.rule: 有没有什么 …: “什么” makes a question softer, and the sentence means the same without it
context.en: Is there anything you want to buy?

why: 有没有什么要买的东西: 什么 means 'any' in this yes/no question.

not.哪儿: 哪儿 means 'where' and doesn't go before 要买的东西.
not.怎么样: 怎么样 means 'how is it' and doesn't go before a noun phrase.
not.为什么: 为什么 means 'why' and doesn't go before a noun phrase.

q: 这个周末你有___打算吗？

context.rule: 有没有什么 …: “什么” makes a question softer, and the sentence means the same without it
context.en: Do you have any plans for this weekend?

why: 有什么打算 means 'any plans': 什么 is soft and indefinite here.

not.谁: 谁 means 'who' and doesn't fit before 打算.
not.几: 几 asks 'how many' and needs a measure word.
not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and doesn't fit before 打算.

q: 这里没___人，我们坐下吧。

context.rule: 有没有什么 …: “什么” makes a question softer, and the sentence means the same without it
context.en: There aren't many people here; let's sit down.

why: 没什么人 means 'not many people': 什么 here softens the negative.

not.多么: 多么 means 'how (very)' and doesn't go before 人.
not.一点: 一点 means 'a bit' and 没一点人 is not natural.
not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and doesn't go before 人.

q: 这个公园漂亮___。

context.rule: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
context.en: This park is extremely beautiful.

why: Adjective + 极了 means 'extremely': 漂亮极了.

not.得极: 得极 is not a pattern; you say 极了 after the adjective.
not.很极: 很极 is not a pattern.
not.太极: 太极 is not a pattern (太极 is 'tai chi').

q: 今天的天气好___，我们去爬山吧。

context.rule: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
context.en: The weather is wonderful today; let's go hiking.

why: 好极了 means 'extremely good': 极了 follows the adjective 好.

not.极是: 极是 is not a pattern.
not.很极: 很极 is not a pattern.
not.太极: 太极 is not a pattern (太极 is 'tai chi').

q: 我妈妈做的菜好吃___。

context.rule: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
context.en: The food my mother makes is extremely tasty.

why: 好吃极了 means 'extremely tasty': 极了 follows the adjective.

not.极是: 极是 is not a pattern.
not.极着: 极着 is not a pattern.
not.极过: 极过 is not a pattern.

q: 听到这个好消息，他高兴___。

context.rule: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
context.en: He was extremely happy to hear the good news.

why: 高兴极了 means 'extremely happy': 极了 follows the adjective.

not.极要: 极要 is not a pattern.
not.极吗: 极吗 is not a pattern; 吗 only makes questions.
not.极呢: 极呢 is not a pattern.

q: 那个电影我喜欢___。

context.rule: Adj / mental verb + 极了: extremely
context.en: I like that film extremely.

why: 喜欢极了 means 'like it extremely': 极了 can follow a verb like 喜欢.

not.极是: 极是 is not a pattern.
not.极吗: 极吗 is not a pattern; 吗 only makes questions.
not.极地: 极地 means 'polar region', not a degree word.

q: ___明天不下雨，我们就去公园。

context.rule: 如果 A，就 B: if A, then B (the subject goes before 就)
context.en: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we'll go to the park.

why: 如果……，我们就……: 如果 means 'if'.

not.因为: 因为 means 'because', but the meaning is conditional.

q: 如果你累了，___去休息吧。

context.rule: 如果 A，就 B: if A, then B (the subject goes before 就)
context.en: If you're tired, go and rest.

why: 如果你累了，就去休息吧: 就 links the 'if' clause to the result.

not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't fit this advice.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't link a result to an 'if'.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and doesn't link a result.

q: 如果我有钱的话，我___买一辆新车。

context.rule: 如果 A，就 B: if A, then B (the subject goes before 就)
context.en: If I had money, I'd buy a new car.

why: 如果……的话，我就买: 就 links the 'if' clause to the result.

not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't suit this meaning.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and doesn't link a result.
not.极: 极 only appears in 极了 and doesn't fit before 买.

q: 如果你喜欢这件衣服，___买吧。

context.rule: 如果 A，就 B: if A, then B (the subject goes before 就)
context.en: If you like these clothes, then buy them.

why: 如果你喜欢，就买吧: 就 links the 'if' clause to the advice.

not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts 如果.
not.却: 却 means 'yet' and contradicts 如果.
not.还: 还 means 'still' and doesn't link an 'if' clause to the result.

q: 如果你有问题，我们___一起想办法。

context.rule: 如果 A，就 B: if A, then B (the subject goes before 就)
context.en: If you have a problem, we'll think of a way together.

why: 如果你有问题，我们就一起想办法: 就 links the 'if' clause to the result.

not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't fit.
not.可是: 可是 means 'but' and contradicts 如果.
not.或者: 或者 means 'or' and doesn't link a result.

q: 听到这个消息，她高兴___哭了。

context.rule: 得 complement of state: 累得 … / 高兴得 …: so … that …
context.en: She was so happy at the news that she cried.

why: 高兴得哭了: 得 links the adjective 高兴 to the result 哭了.

not.的: 的 links a describing word to a noun.
not.地: 地 links an adverb to a verb.
not.了: 了 marks completion and can't link 高兴 to the result.

q: 她累___一回家就睡觉了。

context.rule: 得 complement of state: 累得 … / 高兴得 …: so … that …
context.en: She was so tired that she went to sleep as soon as she got home.

why: 累得一回家就睡觉了: 得 links 累 to the result clause.

not.的: 的 links a describing word to a noun.
not.地: 地 links an adverb to a verb.
not.着: 着 marks an ongoing state and doesn't link a result.

q: 我今天累得___想做饭了。

context.rule: 得 complement of state: 累得 … / 高兴得 …: so … that …
context.en: I'm so tired today that I don't want to cook.

why: 累得不想做饭: 不 makes the result negative, 'don't want to cook'.

not.没: 没 negates 有 or past actions; it doesn't go before 想.
not.别: 别 means 'don't' as a command and doesn't fit a statement.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't say what the tiredness caused.

q: 我忙得___时间吃午饭。

context.rule: 得 complement of state: 累得 … / 高兴得 …: so … that …
context.en: I was so busy that I had no time for lunch.

why: 忙得没时间吃午饭: 没 negates 有 time: 'had no time'.

not.不是: 不是 negates 'to be' and doesn't work before 时间 here.
not.别: 别 means 'don't' as a command and doesn't fit a statement.
not.太: 太 means 'too' and would not negate 时间.

q: 孩子们玩儿得___想回家。

context.rule: 得 complement of state: 累得 … / 高兴得 …: so … that …
context.en: The children were having so much fun that they didn't even want to go home.

why: 玩儿得都不想回家: 都不 shows the extreme result, 'not even wanting to go home'.

not.才: 才 means 'only then' and doesn't give the extreme result.
not.就: 就 means 'then / just' and doesn't give the extreme result.
not.极了: 极了 means 'extremely' and can't go before 想回家.

q: 孩子的手___，很可爱。

context.rule: a one-syllable adjective said twice + 的 paints a more vivid picture
context.en: The child's hands are tiny and lovely.

why: 小小的 is the AA的 form: 孩子的手小小的, tiny and cute.

not.小小: 小小 without 的 can't be a predicate here.
not.很小小的: 很 can't be used with a reduplicated adjective.
not.小了小: 小了小 is not a pattern.

q: 这个孩子的脸___。

context.rule: a one-syllable adjective said twice + 的 paints a more vivid picture
context.en: This child's face is red.

why: 红红的 is the AA的 form: the face is rosy.

not.红的红: 红的红 is not a pattern.
not.红了红: 红了红 is not a pattern.
not.很红红的: 很 can't be used with a reduplicated adjective.

q: 那条河宽宽___，水很干净。

context.rule: a one-syllable adjective said twice + 的 paints a more vivid picture
context.en: That river is wide and the water is clean.

why: 宽宽的 is the AA的 form; 的 closes the reduplicated adjective.

not.得: 得 links a verb to a result and can't close an AA adjective.
not.地: 地 links an adverb to a verb.
not.了: 了 marks a change and doesn't close an AA adjective.

q: 这条路长长___，我们走了很久。

context.rule: a one-syllable adjective said twice + 的 paints a more vivid picture
context.en: This road is so long; we walked for ages.

why: 长长的 is the AA的 form; 的 closes the reduplicated adjective.

not.得: 得 links a verb to a result and can't close an AA adjective.
not.地: 地 links an adverb to a verb.
not.着: 着 marks an ongoing state and can't close an AA adjective.

q: 她的眼睛___，笑起来很好看。

context.rule: a one-syllable adjective said twice + 的 paints a more vivid picture
context.en: Her eyes are big and she looks nice when she smiles.

why: 大大的 is the AA的 form: her eyes are big.

not.大大: 大大 without 的 can't be a predicate here.
not.很大大的: 很 can't be used with a reduplicated adjective.
not.大了大: 大了大 is not a pattern.

q: 你太累了，应该___。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: You're too tired; you should get some rest.

why: 休息休息 is the ABAB form of 休息, meaning 'rest a little'.

not.休休息息: 休休息息 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.休息息休: 休息息休 is not a pattern.
not.休息一息: 休息一息 is not a pattern; it would be 休息一下.

q: 我的作业写完了，你帮我___吧。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: I've finished my homework; please check it for me.

why: 检查检查 is the ABAB form of 检查, meaning 'check it a bit'.

not.检检查查: 检检查查 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.检查查: 检查查 is not a pattern.
not.检一检查: 检一检查 is not a pattern.

q: 他是新同学，你___他吧。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: He's a new classmate; introduce him around.

why: 介绍介绍 is the ABAB form of 介绍, meaning 'introduce a bit'.

not.介介绍绍: 介介绍绍 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.介绍绍: 介绍绍 is not a pattern.
not.绍介绍介: 绍介绍介 is not a pattern.

q: 明天我们一起去公园___。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: Tomorrow let's go to the park and get some exercise.

why: 锻炼锻炼 is the ABAB form of 锻炼, meaning 'get some exercise'.

not.锻锻炼炼: 锻锻炼炼 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.锻炼炼: 锻炼炼 is not a pattern.
not.锻炼了锻: 锻炼了锻 is not a pattern.

q: 这本书不错，你也___吧。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: This book is good; study it a bit too.

why: 学习学习 is the ABAB form of 学习, meaning 'study it a bit'.

not.学学习习: 学学习习 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.学习习: 学习习 is not a pattern.
not.学习了学习: 学习了学习 marks a finished action; a suggestion needs the plain ABAB.

q: 你对他不太了解，可以去___他。

context.rule: ABAB: a short or tentative action, e.g. 休息休息
context.en: You don't know him well; go and get to know him.

why: 认识认识 is the ABAB form of 认识, meaning 'get to know'.

not.认认识识: 认认识识 is not a pattern (the form is ABAB).
not.认识识: 认识识 is not a pattern.
not.识认识认: 识认识认 is not a pattern.

q: 这么晚了，___都不想出门。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: It's so late that nobody wants to go out.

why: 谁都不想出门 means 'nobody wants to go out': 谁……都 covers everyone.

not.什么: 什么 means 'what'; a thing can't want to go out.
not.哪儿: 哪儿 means 'where' and can't be the one who wants.
not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and can't be the one who wants.

q: 周末我___都不想做。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: At the weekend I don't want to do anything.

why: 什么都不想做 means 'don't want to do anything': 什么……都 means 'anything'.

not.谁: 谁 means 'who' and can't be what is done.
not.哪儿: 哪儿 means 'where' and doesn't fit before 做.
not.几: 几 asks 'how many' and needs a measure word.

q: 这个地方很漂亮，___都可以拍照。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: This place is beautiful; you can take photos anywhere.

why: 哪儿都可以拍照 means 'anywhere is fine': 哪儿……都 means 'anywhere'.

not.什么: 什么 means 'what' and doesn't fit the idea of a place.
not.为什么: 为什么 means 'why' and doesn't mean 'anywhere'.
not.几: 几 asks 'how many' and needs a measure word.

q: 你想吃___都行，我请客。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: You can eat whatever you want; it's my treat.

why: 想吃什么都行 means 'whatever you want is fine': 什么……都 means 'anything'.

not.谁: 谁 means 'who' and can't be eaten.
not.怎么: 怎么 means 'how' and doesn't fit after 吃.
not.几: 几 asks 'how many' and needs a measure word.

q: 这个问题太容易了，___都会做。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: This question is so easy that anyone can do it.

why: 谁都会做 means 'anyone can do it': 谁……都 means 'anyone'.

not.哪儿: 哪儿 means 'where' and can't be the one who does it.
not.为什么: 为什么 means 'why' and doesn't mean 'anyone'.
not.怎么样: 怎么样 means 'how is it' and doesn't mean 'anyone'.

q: 我们___去都可以，只要不太晚。

context.rule: question word + 都: every … without exception
context.en: We can go any way you like, as long as it's not too late.

why: 怎么去都可以 means 'any way of going is fine': 怎么……都 means 'any way'.

not.谁: 谁 means 'who' and doesn't fit before 去.
not.哪个: 哪个 means 'which' and needs a noun, not a verb.
not.为什么: 为什么 means 'why' and doesn't mean 'any way'.

q: ___你努力学习，就一定能学好汉语。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as you study hard, you will certainly learn Chinese well.

why: 只要……就……: 只要你努力学习 means 'as long as you study hard'.

q: 只要你有时间，我们___去旅游。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as you have time, we'll go travelling.

why: 只要……就……: 就 follows 只要你有时间 to give the result.

not.才: 才 pairs with 只有, not 只要.
not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts 只要.
not.却: 却 means 'yet' and contradicts 只要.

q: 只要天气好，我们___去公园玩儿。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as the weather is good, we'll go and play in the park.

why: 只要天气好，我们就去公园玩儿: 就 pairs with 只要.

not.而: 而 means 'and / but' and doesn't pair with 只要.
not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts 只要.
not.又: 又 means 'again' and doesn't pair with 只要.

q: 你___想来，什么时候都可以。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as you want to come, any time is fine.

why: 只要你想来，什么时候都可以: 只要 means 'as long as'.

q: 他只要有空，___会来帮我。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as he is free, he will come and help me.

why: 他只要有空，就会来帮我: 就 pairs with 只要.

not.才: 才 pairs with 只有, not 只要.
not.而: 而 means 'and / but' and doesn't pair with 只要.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't link a result.

q: 只要你同意，我___去做。

context.rule: 只要 A，就 B: as long as A, then B
context.en: As long as you agree, I'll do it.

why: 只要你同意，我就去做: 就 pairs with 只要.

not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts 只要.
not.极: 极 only appears in 极了 and doesn't link a result.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't link a result.

q: 我想看一本___中国历史的书。

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: I'd like to read a book about Chinese history.

why: 关于中国历史的书 means 'a book about Chinese history': 关于 introduces the topic.

not.向: 向 means 'toward' and introduces a direction, not a topic.

q: ___这个问题，我们明天再说。

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: As for this question, let's talk tomorrow.

why: 关于这个问题 means 'about this question': 关于 introduces the topic at the start.

not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't introduce a topic.

q: 这是一部___动物的电影。

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: This is a film about animals.

why: 关于动物的电影 means 'a film about animals': 关于 introduces the topic.

not.为了: 为了 means 'in order to' and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.从: 从 means 'from' and doesn't introduce a topic.

q: 我有很多___学习汉语的问题。

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: I have a lot of questions about learning Chinese.

why: 关于学习汉语的问题 means 'questions about learning Chinese': 关于 introduces the topic.

not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.被: 被 marks a passive and doesn't introduce a topic.

q: ___旅游的事，你决定了吗？

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: About the trip: have you decided?

why: 关于旅游的事 means 'about the trip': 关于 introduces the topic.

not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't introduce a topic.

q: 老师给我们讲了一个___世界各国文化的故事。

context.rule: 关于 + noun: about, regarding
context.en: The teacher told us a story about the cultures of countries around the world.

why: 关于世界各国文化的故事 means 'a story about cultures': 关于 introduces the topic.

not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.往: 往 means 'toward' a place and doesn't introduce a topic.
not.离: 离 means 'away from' a place and doesn't introduce a topic.

q: 这个城市___很大，而且很漂亮。

context.rule: 不但 A，而且 B: not only A but also B
context.en: This city is not only big but also beautiful.

why: 不但……而且……: 这个城市不但很大，而且很漂亮 adds a second quality.

not.虽然: 虽然 means 'although' and pairs with 但是.

q: 他不但会唱歌，___会跳舞。

context.rule: 不但 A，而且 B: not only A but also B
context.en: He not only sings but also dances.

why: 不但……，而且……: 他不但会唱歌，而且会跳舞 adds a second skill.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and doesn't pair with 不但.

q: 这家饭馆不但菜好吃，___服务员也很热情。

context.rule: 不但 A，而且 B: not only A but also B
context.en: At this restaurant not only is the food good, the waiters are friendly too.

why: 不但菜好吃，而且服务员也很热情: 而且 pairs with 不但.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and doesn't pair with 不但.

q: 这个城市不但冬天很冷，___夏天也很热。

context.rule: 不但 A，而且 B: not only A but also B
context.en: In this city it's not only cold in winter but hot in summer too.

why: 不但冬天很冷，而且夏天也很热: 而且 pairs with 不但.

not.但是: 但是 means 'but' and doesn't pair with 不但.

q: 我的邻居不但爱唱歌，而且___画画儿。

context.rule: 不但 A，而且 B: not only A but also B
context.en: My neighbour not only loves singing but also drawing.

why: 不但爱唱歌，而且爱画画儿: 爱 repeats the verb after 而且.

not.但: 但 means 'but' and contradicts the pattern.

q: 这个字太难，我写不___。

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: This character is too hard; I can't write it out.

why: 写不出来 means 'can't write it out': 出来 here means producing a result.

not.过去: 过去 means 'go over' and doesn't mean 'write out'.

q: 电话里的人是谁，你听___了吗？

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: Could you tell who was on the phone?

why: 听出来 means 'make out by hearing': 出来 shows you identified who it was.

not.回来: 回来 means 'come back' and doesn't mean 'make out'.
not.起去: 起去 is not a pattern.

q: 他把这个电话号码记___了。

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: He noted the phone number down.

why: 记下来 means 'write down / record': 下来 fixes something in place.

not.出来: 出来 means 'make out', not 'note down'.
not.过来: 过来 means 'come over' and doesn't mean 'note down'.

q: 我终于想___她是谁了，她是我的小学同学。

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: At last I remembered who she is: my primary school classmate.

why: 想起来 means 'recall': 起来 shows a memory coming up.

q: 这件蓝衣服___很漂亮。

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: This blue piece of clothing looks very pretty.

why: 看上去 means 'looks (like)': 上去 here gives an impression.

not.看出来: 看出来 means 'figure out by looking', which needs a different sentence.
not.看下来: 看下来 means 'after watching through' and doesn't mean 'looks'.

q: 老师一进教室，学生们就安静___了。

context.rule: 出来 / 下来 / 起来 / 上去: extended meanings of direction complements
context.en: As soon as the teacher came into the classroom, the students quietened down.

why: 安静下来 means 'quieten down': 下来 shows a change into a calmer state.

q: 每天跑步___我的身体越来越好。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: Running every day makes me healthier and healthier.

why: 使 + person + result: 使我的身体越来越好 means 'makes me healthier'.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.被: 被 marks a passive and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mean 'cause'.

q: 这个好消息___大家都很高兴。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: This good news made everyone happy.

why: 让 + person + feeling: 让大家都很高兴 means 'made everyone happy'.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mean 'cause'.

q: 你___他快点儿来。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: Tell him to come quickly.

why: 叫 + person + verb: 叫他快点儿来 means 'tell him to come quickly'.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'tell'.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mean 'tell someone to'.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mean 'tell someone to'.

q: 老师常常___我们多听多说。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: The teacher often has us listen and speak more.

why: 让 + person + verb: 让我们多听多说 means 'has us listen and speak more'.

not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mean 'have someone do'.
not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'have someone do'.

q: 这条蓝裙子___她看上去更年轻。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: This blue skirt makes her look younger.

why: 使 + person + result: 使她看上去更年轻 means 'makes her look younger'.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mean 'cause'.

q: 晚上喝咖啡会___我睡不着。

context.rule: 使 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb phrase: to make someone …
context.en: Drinking coffee in the evening keeps me awake.

why: 让 + person + result: 让我睡不着 means 'keeps me awake'.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't mean 'cause'.
not.给: 给 means 'to / for' a person and doesn't mean 'cause'.

q: 我的自行车___谁骑走了？

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: Who rode off on my bike?

why: 被 marks the passive: 我的自行车被谁骑走了 means 'by whom was it ridden off'.

not.把: 把 would put 自行车 as the object of a doer, but it is the one acted on.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mark a passive.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: 蛋糕___弟弟吃完了。

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: The cake was all eaten by my younger brother.

why: 被 marks the passive: 蛋糕被弟弟吃完了 means 'was eaten up by my brother'.

not.把: 把 would need the doer first: 弟弟把蛋糕吃完了.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mark a passive.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: 我的作业还没有___老师检查呢。

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: My homework hasn't been checked by the teacher yet.

why: 被 marks the passive: 还没有被老师检查 means 'not yet checked by the teacher'.

not.把: 把 would need the doer first.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mark a passive.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: 我昨天买的书___朋友借走了。

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: The book I bought yesterday was borrowed by a friend.

why: 被 marks the passive: 书被朋友借走了 means 'was borrowed by a friend'.

not.把: 把 would need the doer first: 朋友把书借走了.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mark a passive.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: 窗户___风刮开了。

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: The window was blown open by the wind.

why: 被 marks the passive: 窗户被风刮开了 means 'was blown open by the wind'.

not.把: 把 would need the doer first: 风把窗户刮开了.
not.为: 为 means 'for' or 'because of' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: 照相机已经___弟弟用坏了。

context.rule: S + 被 + (agent) + verb + other element: the passive
context.en: The camera has already been broken by my younger brother.

why: 被 marks the passive: 照相机被弟弟用坏了 means 'was broken by my brother'.

not.把: 把 would need the doer first: 弟弟把照相机用坏了.
not.向: 向 means 'toward' and doesn't mark a passive.
not.在: 在 means 'at / in' and doesn't mark a passive.

q: ___你每天练习，才能提高水平。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: Only if you practise every day can you improve your level.

why: 只有……才……: 只有你每天练习，才能提高 means 'only if you practise'.

not.只要: 只要 means 'as long as' and pairs with 就, not 才.
not.如果: 如果 means 'if' and pairs with 就.

q: 只有周末，他___有时间打篮球。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: Only at the weekend does he have time to play basketball.

why: 只有周末，他才有时间: 才 pairs with 只有.

not.就: 就 pairs with 只要, not 只有.
not.都: 都 means 'all' and doesn't pair with 只有.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't pair with 只有.

q: 只有努力，才___有机会。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: Only by working hard can you get opportunities.

why: 只有努力，才能有机会: 才 + 能 pairs with 只有.

not.把: 把 is an object marker and doesn't fit after 才.
not.被: 被 marks a passive and doesn't fit after 才.
not.对: 对 means 'to / towards' and doesn't fit after 才.

q: 只有自己去过，你___能知道那儿有多漂亮。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: Only if you go yourself can you know how beautiful it is.

why: 只有自己去过，你才能知道: 才 pairs with 只有.

not.就: 就 pairs with 只要, not 只有.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't pair with 只有.
not.还: 还 means 'still' and doesn't pair with 只有.

q: 这个问题很难，只有王老师___能回答。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: This question is hard; only Teacher Wang can answer it.

why: 只有王老师才能回答: 才 pairs with 只有.

not.就: 就 pairs with 只要, not 只有.
not.却: 却 means 'yet' and doesn't pair with 只有.
not.也: 也 means 'also' and doesn't pair with 只有.

q: ___认真学习，成绩才能提高。

context.rule: 只有 A，才 B: only if A, then B
context.en: Only if you study seriously can your grades improve.

why: 只有认真学习，成绩才能提高: 只有 pairs with 才.

not.只要: 只要 means 'as long as' and pairs with 就, not 才.
not.如果: 如果 means 'if' and pairs with 就.
